description: #res numbers the reserve rows with ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY period, claim_id ORDER BY reserve_date DESC, reserve_id DESC) and keeps rn = 1. That leaves one reserve row per claim and period. A claim usually holds an indemnity reserve and an expense reserve (CR-0577). Only the most recently changed of the two goes into outstanding_reserve, and the other type's open reserve is dropped. This understates outstanding_reserve, incurred_amount, incurred_90d_ago and movement_90d. It can also keep claims off the list entirely or give them the wrong watch_category.

impact.query: WITH clm AS (SELECT claim_id FROM stg_claims WHERE reported_date <= DATE'2025-12-31' AND (upper(rtrim(status)) <> 'CLOSED' OR closed_date > DATE'2025-10-02')), paid AS (SELECT p.claim_id, SUM(COALESCE(p.amount,0)) AS paid_now, SUM(CASE WHEN p.payment_date <= DATE'2025-10-02' THEN COALESCE(p.amount,0) ELSE 0 END) AS paid_prior FROM stg_claim_payments p JOIN clm c ON c.claim_id = p.claim_id WHERE p.payment_date <= DATE'2025-12-31' GROUP BY p.claim_id), res AS (SELECT r.claim_id, r.reserve_amount, d.period, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY d.period, r.claim_id ORDER BY r.reserve_date DESC, r.reserve_id DESC) AS rn_leg, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY d.period, r.claim_id, r.reserve_type ORDER BY r.reserve_date DESC, r.reserve_id DESC) AS rn_int FROM stg_claim_reserves r JOIN clm c ON c.claim_id = r.claim_id CROSS JOIN (SELECT 'NOW' AS period, DATE'2025-12-31' AS as_at UNION ALL SELECT 'PRIOR' AS period, DATE'2025-10-02' AS as_at) d WHERE r.reserve_date <= d.as_at), os AS (SELECT claim_id, COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN period='NOW' AND rn_leg=1 THEN reserve_amount END),0) AS leg_now, COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN period='PRIOR' AND rn_leg=1 THEN reserve_amount END),0) AS leg_prior, COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN period='NOW' AND rn_int=1 THEN reserve_amount END),0) AS int_now, COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN period='PRIOR' AND rn_int=1 THEN reserve_amount END),0) AS int_prior FROM res GROUP BY claim_id), cmp AS (SELECT c.claim_id, COALESCE(p.paid_now,0) + COALESCE(o.leg_now,0) AS leg_inc, COALESCE(p.paid_now,0) + COALESCE(o.int_now,0) AS int_inc, COALESCE(p.paid_prior,0) + COALESCE(o.leg_prior,0) AS leg_prior_inc, COALESCE(p.paid_prior,0) + COALESCE(o.int_prior,0) AS int_prior_inc FROM clm c LEFT JOIN paid p ON p.claim_id = c.claim_id LEFT JOIN os o ON o.claim_id = c.claim_id) SELECT COUNT(*) AS rows_affected, COALESCE(SUM(ABS(int_inc - leg_inc)),0) AS amount_affected FROM cmp WHERE (leg_inc >= 25000 OR int_inc >= 25000) AND (leg_inc <> int_inc OR leg_prior_inc <> int_prior_inc)

intended_behaviour: Take the latest reserve for each claim, period and reserve_type (add reserve_type to the PARTITION BY), then add up those latest amounts across types to get the outstanding reserve. This is how expense reserves become part of incurred, as CR-0577 asks.
title: Latest reserve picked across all reserve types, so only one type counts

description: The claim filter keeps closed claims only when closed_date > @PriorDate, where @PriorDate is AsOfDate - 90 days (2025-10-02). A claim closed on 2025-10-02, exactly 90 days before the as-of date, is therefore left out.

impact.query: WITH clm AS (SELECT claim_id FROM stg_claims WHERE reported_date <= DATE'2025-12-31' AND upper(rtrim(status)) = 'CLOSED' AND closed_date = DATE'2025-10-02'), paid AS (SELECT p.claim_id, SUM(COALESCE(p.amount,0)) AS paid_now FROM stg_claim_payments p JOIN clm c ON c.claim_id = p.claim_id WHERE p.payment_date <= DATE'2025-12-31' GROUP BY p.claim_id), res AS (SELECT r.claim_id, r.reserve_amount, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY r.claim_id ORDER BY r.reserve_date DESC, r.reserve_id DESC) AS rn FROM stg_claim_reserves r JOIN clm c ON c.claim_id = r.claim_id WHERE r.reserve_date <= DATE'2025-12-31'), os AS (SELECT claim_id, COALESCE(SUM(reserve_amount),0) AS os_now FROM res WHERE rn = 1 GROUP BY claim_id), inc AS (SELECT c.claim_id, COALESCE(p.paid_now,0) + COALESCE(o.os_now,0) AS incurred FROM clm c LEFT JOIN paid p ON p.claim_id = c.claim_id LEFT JOIN os o ON o.claim_id = c.claim_id) SELECT COUNT(*) AS rows_affected, COALESCE(SUM(incurred),0) AS amount_affected FROM inc WHERE incurred >= 25000

intended_behaviour: CR-0912 drops claims closed more than 90 days ago. A claim closed exactly 90 days ago should stay on the list (closed_date >= @PriorDate).
title: Claims closed exactly 90 days ago are dropped

description: Line 59 compares the untrimmed c.status with 'CLOSED'. SQL Server ignores trailing spaces and, under the usual collation, case, but it does not ignore leading spaces. A status such as ' CLOSED' passes the <> 'CLOSED' test, so claims closed long ago (or with no closed_date) still make the list. They then appear as 'CLOSED' because the output column is trimmed (INC-3204).
